_comment: PSMutant tested against ITSELF (dogfooding). Every source file is mutated except src/PSMutation.Sandbox.ps1, and that one exclusion is structural rather than a gap: its covering suite tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1 calls Clear-PSMutationStaleSandbox for real, a self-mutation baseline runs IN-PROCESS so it shares $PID with the sandbox the run is executing from, and the sweep treats its own process id as reclaimable -- so naming that suite anywhere here deletes the live run's sandbox mid-baseline and turns the run red before a single mutant is tried. Its behaviour is pinned by the normal suite at 100% line coverage instead. NOTE: this exclusion previously cited a 'shared sandbox' (issue #2, since fixed) and then 'real temp side-effects', neither of which was the actual blocker. Run: Invoke-PSMutation -ConfigFile ./psmutant.self.config.json -SourceRoot .
_sandboxSubtreesComment: schemas/ is copied because the module READS it at run time now: the config schema is the config format, and a sandboxed copy of src/ that cannot find it refuses every config, turning the baseline red before a mutant is tried.
_equivalentsComment: Mutants that provably cannot change behaviour, excluded from the denominator so the score means 'every catchable fault is caught'. Each needs a reason, and the run FAILS if one is ever killed or stops existing - a declaration is a checkable claim, not a mute button. Everything else here was killed by a test; nothing is listed merely because it was inconvenient. ONE DECLARATION RETIRED IN #3: `$isDeclared -> $true` in Get-PSMutationScore argued that counting undeclared keys into $matched could not be observed, because $matched is only read for keys that are declared. True when written. It stopped being true when the key became $null for an undeclared mutant -- $matched[$null] throws -- so the suite now kills all three of those mutants and the claim was removed rather than re-keyed. A declaration is a checkable claim, and this is what it looks like when one stops being needed.

equivalents.src/PSMutation.Report.ps1:Save-PSMutatio: ConvertTo-Json -Depth N and -Depth N+1 emit byte-identical output for any object graph shallower than N. Both report shapes nest 4 deep at their worst (root -> mutants[] -> row -> scalar), so 6 and 7 cannot differ. Killing this would need a fixture built for no purpose but to out-nest the serializer, which would assert nothing about the report. ONE DECLARATION, NOT TWO: this used to be declared separately against Write-PSMutationReport and Write-PSMutationRecheckReport, which held a copy each of the same write. Both went stale the moment the write moved into one function -- the run said so, naming them -- which is the function-keyed form working as intended.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Report.ps1:Get-PSMutation: An early return, not a decision. With $Equivalents null, $null.PSObject is null and so is .Properties, so the foreach below runs zero times and returns the same empty map the guard returns directly - verified by running the loop with the guard removed. Forcing the condition false therefore cannot change the output for any input. (Forcing it TRUE is killed: it would return an empty map even when declarations exist.)
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Config.ps1:Get-PSMutation: ConvertTo-Json -Depth N and -Depth N+1 emit byte-identical output for any object graph shallower than N. A config nests 3 deep at its worst (root -> tests -> file -> array of strings), so 10 and 11 cannot differ. The depth is 10 rather than the default 2 because the default TRUNCATES silently, and a truncated config would validate against the schema as though the missing part were absent; killing this mutant would need a config built to out-nest the serialiser, which no real config can be.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Operators.ps1:Get-PSMutat: The default clause here assigns $null -- `default { $null }` -- which is exactly what a switch yields when NOTHING matches. Forcing the clause never to match therefore produces the same $flip for the same input, and `if (-not $flip) { continue }` takes the same branch. Exposed by 0.4.0 teaching ConditionForcing to reach `default` at all; it is this module's own source being measured by its own new operator, and the mutant is equivalent by construction rather than untested. The OTHER direction is not declared and is killed: forcing `{ $true }` makes the default match alongside the specific clause, and a switch collects every matched clause, so $flip becomes a two-element array and the emitted mutant text changes.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Pester.ps1:<script-body>:: $script:PSMutationWarmUses starts at 0 and is compared with -ge against a fixed interval, so starting it at 1 recycles the warm runspace one mutant earlier and changes nothing a caller can observe -- the runspace is rebuilt on a schedule precisely because nothing depends on WHICH mutant triggers it. KEYED BY <script-body>, NOT BY LINE, and that is the fix for #179 rather than a style choice. This declaration was re-keyed twice in one day -- 154 -> 167 -> 181 -- by two unrelated edits to docstrings above it, the second comment-only. A file-scope mutant has no enclosing function to name, so it used to keep only the line form and churned on every edit above it. It now answers to the same synthetic the sibling uses for a unit with no function.
